newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas rallies late, ends near new highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas rallies late, ends near new highs.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures staged a late rally Thursday and ended very near new contract highs, driven by forecasts for cold weather and concerns about storage after Wednesday's bullish AGA data, sources said.

January surged 27.9 cents to close at $3.784 per million British thermal units after hitting a new contract high of $3.80. February, which also rallied to a new high of $3.42, settled 25 cents higher at $3.406. Others also ended up.
"Fundamentally, the market looks pretty good, but it may have (temporarily) outpaced itself. I think we're overdue for a correction," said one East Coast trader.

Most agreed the market was overbought and due for a pullback after a 16 percent rally in three sessions, but longer-term, they said more gains were likely, particularly with stocks low and colder weather ahead.
Temperatures in the East were expected to dip to below-normal through early next week, but forecasters were mixed on the 10-15 day outlook.
AGA reported Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks fell last week by 104 bcf, well-above expectations in the 70-80 bcf range. Stocks are now 217 bcf, or 8.1 percent, below year-ago.

Technical traders pegged minor support in January in the $3.50 area, with major support at $3.10 and then at $3.04, a low from November 21. Resistance was seen at the new high of $3.80, then at the December expiration of $3.901 and then at the all-time spot continuation high of $4.05 hit November 21.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices climbed almost 20 cents Thursday to the mid-to-high $3.80s. Midcontinent pipes were up almost a dime to the high-$3.60s. New York city gate gas climbed into the $4.70s early, then slipped back to the $4.50s, up 15 cents or more on the day.
The 12-month strip jumped 13.3 cents to $2.604. NYMEX said 43,596 Hub contracts traded, up from Wednesday's revised tally of 38,198.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas finished unchanged at $1.75, with February also closing steady at $1.65. NYMEX said one Alberta contract traded versus seven on Wednesday.
NYMEX Permian natgas again was untraded, with January settling unchanged at $3.00.
On the KCBT, January ended 28.5 cents higher at $3.615, while deferreds closed 10 to 24 cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.6 cent to 16.9 cents (NYMEX premium).
